title: Episode 251: Sean Parent C++ Under the Sea Keynote Preview

sentences.en: So you got me, you got AI, you're good.
sentences.zh: 所以你算拿捏我了，你也拿捏了AI，你挺厉害。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's all we need.
sentences.zh: 对，这就是我们需要的一切。

sentences.en: That's all we need.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们需要的一切。

sentences.en: And you talking about AI.
sentences.zh: 而且你在谈论AI。

sentences.en: That's the third pillar right there.
sentences.zh: 这就是第三大支柱。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 251, recorded on August 21st, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到ADSP播客第251期，录制于2025年8月21日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳。

sentences.en: And today with my co-host, Bryce, we interview Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 今天我和我的联合主持布莱斯一起采访肖恩·帕伦特。

sentences.en: This is part four of a four-part conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是四部分对话的第四部分。

sentences.en: You heard part three last week.
sentences.zh: 你上周听了第三部分。

sentences.en: We're doing part four this week, and then you'll hear the first two parts in the next two episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们这周进行第四部分，然后你会在接下来两期节目中听到前两部分。

sentences.en: In this episode, we chat with Sean about his upcoming keynote talk at C++ Under the Sea.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们和肖恩聊了他在“C++深海”大会上的即将发表的主旨演讲。

sentences.en: You are going to be keynoting in T-Minus-A-Month.
sentences.zh: 你将在倒计时一个月时发表主旨演讲。

sentences.en: I don't think they've announced the other speakers yet.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们还没宣布其他演讲嘉宾呢。

sentences.en: No, they have not.
sentences.zh: 对，还没宣布。

sentences.en: They have not.
sentences.zh: 还没呢。

sentences.en: So tell us briefly what you'll be chatting about.
sentences.zh: 那么请简要告诉我们你要聊些什么。

sentences.en: And I think the dates are like October 9th and 10th.
sentences.zh: 日期大概是10月9日和10日吧。

sentences.en: So if folks are in Europe or close or willing to fly to the Netherlands, you can go see Sean's talk.
sentences.zh: 所以如果大家在欧洲、附近或者愿意飞往荷兰，可以去听听肖恩的演讲。

sentences.en: This is current Connor while he is editing this episode, which we recorded on August 21St.
sentences.zh: 这是康纳在剪辑本期节目时的插话，我们是在8月21日录制这期的。

sentences.en: And since we recorded, Bryce and I both had our talks accepted to C++ Under the Sea.
sentences.zh: 在我们录制之后，我和布莱斯的演讲都被“C++深海”大会接受了。

sentences.en: So not only can you go and see Sean and get to chat with him at C++ Under the Sea, Bryce and I will also be there.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅你可以去“C++深海”大会看肖恩并和他交流，我和布莱斯也都会去。

sentences.en: So if you're not going to be near or close to Copenhagen or in Norway for NDC TechTown, we will also be in Breda, Netherlands on October 9th and 10th.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不在哥本哈根附近、或者没去挪威参加NDC TechTown，我们也会在10月9日和10日出现在荷兰布雷达。

sentences.en: Back to Sean.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，聊回肖恩。

sentences.en: But yeah, what are you going to be talking about?
sentences.zh: 不过，你打算聊些什么呢？

sentences.en: I'm going to repeat the talk that I just gave at C++ Now, which is titled Are We There
sentences.zh: 我打算重复我刚刚在C++ Now大会上的演讲，题目是“我们到了

sentences.en: Yet?
And the title comes from a talk I gave at the very first, it was a keynote at the very first BoostCon pre-C++ Now.
sentences.zh: 这个标题源自我当年在第一届BoostCon（C++ Now前身）上做的一个演讲，那是第一届的主题演讲。

sentences.en: And there's an online recording of it because I also gave it at Google as a Google Tech talk in, I don't know what year it was.
sentences.zh: 网上有录像，因为我也曾在谷歌做过谷歌技术演讲，具体是哪年我记不清了。

sentences.en: So I would have to look it up, 2007, something like that.
sentences.zh: 我得去查一下，2007年，差不多那样吧。

sentences.en: And that talk was titled A Possible Future of Software Development.
sentences.zh: 那场演讲的题目是《软件开发的一个可能未来》。

sentences.en: And basically what it laid out at the time was that there was a huge reduction possible if we moved to generic programming, kind of stepping off style generic programming, and
sentences.zh: 它当时基本上阐明了这样一点：如果我们转向泛型编程——那种逐步淡出风格的泛型编程——将会实现巨大的精简，

sentences.en: we start writing code in terms of algebraic structures so that it can be commonplace.
sentences.zh: 并且我们开始用代数结构来编写代码，这样它就能变得司空见惯。

sentences.en: And that gets rid of a lot of the write and rewrite and rewrite and rewrite and rewrite the same implementation of an algorithm.
sentences.zh: 这就省去了大量编写、重写、再重写、再重写、再重写同一种算法实现的麻烦。

sentences.en: And actually leads to code reuse where object-oriented programming had that promise, but it was never fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 并且实际上带来了代码重用，而面向对象编程虽然曾有过这种承诺，但从未兑现过。

sentences.en: And then started to look at where do we go from here?
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始思考：接下来我们要去向何方？

sentences.en: And the idea of where we go from here is what I refer to as declarative forms, this notion of you should be able to state your intent around how a program is constructed, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对“接下来去向何方”的想法，就是我所说的声明式形式，也就是你应该能够阐明你对程序如何构建的意图，对吧？

sentences.en: So basically you define things structurally and the computer figures out what the right data structures and algorithms are to use to realize that.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上你是从结构上定义事物，然后由计算机找出实现该目标所需的正确数据结构和算法。

sentences.en: And I showed a demo at the time of property models and a UI layout library that I had at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时演示了属性模型以及我当时拥有的一个UI布局库。

sentences.en: I think the property model work is still somewhat unique in the industry.
sentences.zh: 我认为属性模型的工作在业界至今仍有些独特之处。

sentences.en: I've published a number of papers on it with Yanko Yarve.
sentences.zh: 我与扬科·亚维就此发表了多篇论文。

sentences.en: So those are all linked on my website.
sentences.zh: 这些都在我的网站上有链接。

sentences.en: Layout libraries at the time, you know, it was known as EVE, had quite a unique set of capabilities.
sentences.zh: 当时的布局库，你知道的，被称为EVE，具备相当独特的一套功能。

sentences.en: I think less so now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在没那么独特了。

sentences.en: There's a couple of unique capabilities it has.
sentences.zh: 它仍然有一些独特的功能。

sentences.en: It can do cross-hierarchy alignment easily where other layout engines don't.
sentences.zh: 它可以轻松实现跨层级对齐，而其他布局引擎做不到这一点。

sentences.en: But that was kind of a take on it.
sentences.zh: 但这算是对它的一种看法吧。

sentences.en: And so this talk kind of revisits that.
sentences.zh: 所以这次演讲算是对那次的回顾。

sentences.en: How far has generic programming come in the last 20 years?
sentences.zh: 过去20年里，泛型编程发展到了什么地步？

sentences.en: The answer is a lot.
sentences.zh: 答案是发展很大。

sentences.en: Nobody knew what it was 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 20年前根本没人知道那是什么。

sentences.en: And now it's a significant part of all the major languages.
sentences.zh: 而现在它已经成为所有主流语言的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: It is amazing to think about that just 20 years ago, how different the software industry was in that way.
sentences.zh: 想到就在短短20年前，软件行业在这一点上是如此不同，真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Because it's something that Connor and I think take for granted because we sort of grew up in that environment.
sentences.zh: 因为这是我和康纳觉得理所当然的事情，毕竟我们差不多是在那种环境中成长起来的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think there are still things that the industry gets wrong about generic programming.
sentences.zh: 我认为业界对泛型编程仍然存在一些误解。

sentences.en: So I'll touch on some of those.
sentences.zh: 所以我也会谈到其中的一些。

sentences.en: You know, and then this notion of how do we get to declarative forms, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，还有“我们如何走向声明式形式”这个概念，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, at one point, this idea, it's not unique to me, was referred to as like fourth generation languages.
sentences.zh: 你知道，曾经一度，这个想法——并非我独创——被称为第四代语言。

sentences.en: Prologue kind of being the canonical example.
sentences.zh: Prolog算是典型的例子。

sentences.en: And I think the idea was right, but all of these systems have failed for a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个想法是对的，但所有这些系统都由于各种原因失败了。

sentences.en: And so let's look at kind of the reasons why this tact has failed in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们来看看这种策略过去失败的原因。

sentences.en: And can we take another stab at it and maybe go in a different direction?
sentences.zh: 我们能再尝试一次，也许往不同的方向发展吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that declarative languages like that are more relevant these days because of AI?
sentences.zh: 你认为由于AI的出现，这类声明式语言在当今更具相关性了吗？

sentences.en: I think potentially they are.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有可能是的。

sentences.en: Like one of the things that I'm looking at in my current work is how do I expose the structure directly to the AI?
sentences.zh: 比如我目前工作中正在研究的事情之一，就是如何将结构直接暴露给AI？

sentences.en: Another group at Adobe has been doing work on a similar area.
sentences.zh: Adobe的另一个团队一直在相似的领域进行研究。

sentences.en: And that gets really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这变得非常有趣。

sentences.en: It means that you can have your AI build features that weren't there under the hood, right?
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以让AI构建那些底层原本不存在的功能，对吧？

sentences.en: They can play with the Lego blocks, if you will, you know, more at a user level than at a raw coding level.
sentences.zh: 你可以说它们在玩乐高积木，更多是在用户层面而不是在底层编码层面进行操作。

sentences.en: Wasn't Prologue like originally developed by an AI lab back in the 70s?
sentences.zh: Prolog难道不是70年代由某个AI实验室最初开发的吗？

sentences.en: You know, I do not know that.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，这我还真不知道。

sentences.en: I would have to look that up.
sentences.zh: 我得去查一下。

sentences.en: Certainly, it's got early AI.
sentences.zh: 当然，它包含早期AI技术。

sentences.en: It was created around 1972 by some guy from the University of France and their artificial intelligence group.
sentences.zh: 它大约在1972年由法国一所大学的某个家伙和他们的11人工智能小组创建的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So, I think these things connect well to AI and I think potentially solve a lot of the problems of AI.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这些东西与AI紧密相连，并且我认为它们有可能解决AI的许多问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, what my goal is, is to say that, you know, you want to build a set of domain-specific languages as well that all interoperate,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我的目标是说，你希望构建一套能够互操作的领域特定语言，

sentences.en: as well as the infrastructure to define new languages within that family.
sentences.zh: 以及在该系列中定义新语言的基础设施。

sentences.en: And each of the languages, the goal should be to solve a particular class of problems well and to be as provable as possible.
sentences.zh: 每种语言的目标都应该是很好地解决特定类别的问体，并尽可能具备可验证性。

sentences.en: And so, like one of the attributes of the layout system that I did, it's a constraint-based system, but you can neither over-constrain it or under-constrain it.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如我做的布局系统的属性之一，它是一个基于约束的系统，但你既不会过度约束它，也不会约束不足。

sentences.en: Any layout that you describe, it will give a layout.
sentences.zh: 你描述的任何布局，它都能给出一个布局。

sentences.en: And I tried to do the same with property models and fell a little bit short.
sentences.zh: 我试图在属性模型上也做到这一点，但稍微差了一点。

sentences.en: There is a model checker where if you run the model checker and it succeeds, then you know that there's a solution for any set of values that you feed into the system.
sentences.zh: 有一个模型检查器，如果你运行它并且成功了，那么你就知道你输入系统的任何一组值都有解决方案。

sentences.en: The problem is, 20 years ago at the time, I did kind of a back-of-the-envelope proof of the complexity of the model checker and said,
sentences.zh: 问题是，20年前当时，我对模型检查器的复杂度做了一个粗略的证明，然后说，

sentences.en: eh, it looks like it's N log N-ish, something like that.
sentences.zh: 额，看起来大概是N乘以log N之类的。

sentences.en: I recently pulled up those notes and found several mistakes.
sentences.zh: 我最近翻出那些笔记，发现里面有几个错误。

sentences.en: And it's like, no, it's N choose M-ish, which is a whole different version.
sentences.zh: 情况是，不，它是N中选M级别的，这是一个完全不同的版本。

sentences.en: So, it's probably only reasonable to fully model check things at a small scale.
sentences.zh: 所以，全面对小规模之外的事物进行模型检查可能才比较合理。

sentences.en: So, I'm looking at how do you build a system that can do a better job at model checking above that.
sentences.zh: 因此我正在研究如何构建一个系统，以便在此之上更好地进行模型检查。

sentences.en: But, yeah, you know, I think if you, you know, when you write code, if you've ever had the sense of I'm writing kind of the same thing again, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，你知道，如果你在写代码时，有没有过这种感觉：“我又在写同样的东西了”，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm solving a similar problem that falls into a family of problems I've had before.
sentences.zh: 我正在解决一个相似的问题，它属于我以前遇到过的问题族。

sentences.en: Then this notion of how do you back up and how do you describe that class of problems?
sentences.zh: 那么如何退一步并描述那类问题呢？

sentences.en: And how do you get to the point where you can solve it once gets interesting.
sentences.zh: 以及如何达到能够一劳永逸解决它的地步，这就变得很有意思了。

sentences.en: So, that's the direction of the talk.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是演讲的方向。

sentences.en: I'm hoping to get a demo together of my new work right now.
sentences.zh: 我希望现在能把我新工作的演示整合到一起。

sentences.en: There's, I could show a bunch of Rust code, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 我本可以展示一堆Rust代码，但现在还不行。

sentences.en: So, wait, wait, to be clear, your plan for your keynote at the C++ conference is to show a bunch of Rust code.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，明确一下，你C++大会主旨演讲的计划是展示一堆Rust代码。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not saying that's inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不是说这不合适。

sentences.en: I just want to be clear.
sentences.zh: 我只是想弄清楚。

sentences.en: My plan is hopefully to show a demo of a small slice of a functioning system.
sentences.zh: 我的计划是希望能展示一个正常运行系统的一小部分的演示。

sentences.en: If I were to, you know, the closest I could give right now is be like, oh, look at all this Rust code I've written.
sentences.zh: 如果我要这么做的话，我目前能给出的最接近的东西就是：“哦，看看我写的所有这些Rust代码。”

sentences.en: And if I run it on the command line, it puts out these numbers, which are somewhat interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 如果我在命令行上运行它，它就会输出这些数字，这对我来说有点意思。

sentences.en: So, if I'm only at that point still, I won't give a demo.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我当时还处于那种阶段，我就不会做演示。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be interesting.
sentences.zh: 那将毫无吸引力。

sentences.en: You know, I could give a demo at a Rust conference and talk about the structure of the code, and that might be interesting, but not at a C++.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以在Rust大会上做演示并讨论代码结构，那可能会很有趣，但在C++大会上不行。

sentences.en: I have learned that running concurrently with CPP Under the Sea, there is a big AI conference in Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，与“C++深海”同时进行的，在阿姆斯特丹还有一个大型AI大会。

sentences.en: I can't remember the name.
sentences.zh: 我记不清名字了。

sentences.en: World AI Summit.
sentences.zh: 世界AI峰会。

sentences.en: Amsterdam, maybe, is the...
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特丹，也许是……

sentences.en: Interesting name.
sentences.zh: 有趣的名字。

sentences.en: Yes, it's on the 8th and the 9th.
sentences.zh: 是的，在8号和9号。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's some potential crossover there.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那里有一些潜在的交集。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then, you know, for your European listeners, before C++ Under the Sea,
sentences.zh: 然后呢，对于你的欧洲听众来说，在“C++深海”大会之前，

sentences.en: Sergei Platinov has invited me to do a meetup.
sentences.zh: 谢尔盖·普拉蒂诺夫邀请我办一个线下聚会。

sentences.en: And so, I will do probably the same talk in person in a meetup in Zurich.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能会在苏黎世的一个线下聚会上亲自做同样的演讲。

sentences.en: I'll stop by Zurich on my way to the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 我会在去荷兰的路上顺道拜访苏黎世。

sentences.en: For people who don't know Sergei, he's the person who started C++ Russia.
sentences.zh: 对于不认识谢尔盖的人，他就是发起C++ Russia的人。

sentences.en: And when the Russian-Ukraine war broke out, his wife is Ukrainian.
sentences.zh: 当俄乌战争爆发时，他的妻子是乌克兰人。

sentences.en: And he fled the country and now it's in Zurich, which was very sad.
sentences.zh: 他逃离了国家，现在在苏黎世，这非常令人难过。

sentences.en: The day before the war broke out, he sent me an invite to speak at C++ Russia again.
sentences.zh: 就在战争爆发的前一天，他还给我发了邀请函，让我再次在C++ Russia上发言。

sentences.en: Uh-uh.
sentences.zh: 呃呃。

sentences.en: That was a good conference.
sentences.zh: 那是个很棒的会议。

sentences.en: It's a shame.
sentences.zh: 真是个遗憾。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The reason, though, I was saying that is we had such a blast at C++ on C...
sentences.zh: 不过我之所以这么说，是因为我们在C++ on C……上玩得太开心了

sentences.en: I want to say it was 2023 at this point, because I...
sentences.zh: 我想那应该是2023年，因为我……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Was it 2023?
I think it must have been, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我觉得一定是，是的。

sentences.en: It was either...
sentences.zh: 要么是……

sentences.en: It was either...
sentences.zh: 要么是……

sentences.en: It definitely wasn't this year.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是今年。

sentences.en: So, it was either 24 or 23.
sentences.zh: 所以要么是24年，要么是23年。

sentences.en: But anyways, it was a blast recording in person, you know, during the dinner, post-dinner.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，在线下录音时——你知道的，在晚餐期间、晚餐后——真是太爽了。

sentences.en: And if it's not at C++ Under the Sea, we will try to have to make that happen in person again.
sentences.zh: 如果不是在“C++深海”上，我们会尽量再次在线下实现这一点。

sentences.en: Because as fun as it...
sentences.zh: 因为不管它有多……

sentences.en: I mean, this was amazing, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，老实说，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I don't know how you've managed to bundle so many, like, internet happy topics.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是怎么设法把这么多互联网上开心的话题捆绑在一起的。

sentences.en: We've got Rust versus C++.
sentences.zh: 我们有Rust对决C++。

sentences.en: We've got AI.
sentences.zh: 我们有AI。

sentences.en: And we've got, like, the dystopic or utopic future that lays ahead for us, should people be worried or not.
sentences.zh: 我们还有摆在我们面前的、反乌托邦或乌托邦式的未来，人们是否应该担心。

sentences.en: So, this is just going to be banger after banger.
sentences.zh: 所以这简直是一个接一个的王炸。

sentences.en: But yeah, as fun as this was, we will have to try to do this again in person at some point.

sentences.zh: 确实有很多会议，我倒是不介意……你知道的，就是那种仅仅因为政治原因需要我露个脸才要求我出席的会议。

sentences.en: And it's like, just put an avatar for me in there and I'll go write some code.
sentences.zh: 那种情况下，放个我的虚拟形象在那儿就行了，我好去写点代码。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 走着瞧吧。

sentences.en: We might be living in that future soon because we can all think of examples of that where, yeah, whether it's meetings or something.
sentences.zh: 我们可能很快就会生活在那种未来了，因为我们都能想到类似的例子，无论是会议还是其他什么事情。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We'll let you go then, Sean.
sentences.zh: 那我们就先不打扰你了，肖恩。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
